problem: Navigation instruction generation (NIG) methods either map past observations directly to text on limited data, lacking 3D spatial understanding, or use LLMs that ignore global spatial context such as the discretized map structure, and tend to hallucinate landmarks.
motivation: NIG gives embodied agents the ability to give feedback and guidance to humans in natural language, which is needed for human-machine collaboration. Feeding textual map descriptions to LLMs is a shallow way to use spatial context, so the paper injects map context directly through parameter-efficient prompt tuning.
key_idea: MAPInstructor encodes egocentric observations into 3D voxel scene representations, integrates a topological map of the whole trajectory into an LLM decoder via map prompt tuning, and uses landmark uncertainty assessment to reduce hallucinated landmarks.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that map context injected as prompts (rather than as text) and uncertainty-aware landmark prediction improve the reliability and coherence of generated instructions.
method: Scene representation encoding: projects egocentric observations into 3D voxels for fine-grained scene understanding.
Map prompt tuning: integrates a topological map representation of the entire trajectory into an LLM-based decoder for parameter-efficient updating.
Landmark uncertainty assessment: mitigates hallucination in landmark predictions to improve the reliability and coherence of instructions.

setting.backbone: LLM-based decoder (specific model not stated in abstract), parameter-efficient prompt-tuned
setting.training_data: R2R, REVERIE, RxR instruction datasets (details not given in abstract)
setting.observation: egocentric observations projected to 3D voxels; topological map of the trajectory

results: The abstract states that extensive experiments on R2R, REVERIE and RxR confirm the generalization and effectiveness of MAPInstructor, with no numbers given.
limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative results or ablations available.
Depends on a trajectory-level topological map and 3D voxel projection, which adds pipeline complexity.
